candidates.summary: the stamped bench that sets objectInfo's flat 1200 price passes a TypedValue with no T, so declaredTypeName returns early and the typed path every production call takes is never measured
candidates.failure_scenario: BenchmarkNative_Reflect_ObjectInfo_Stamped stores gno.TypedValue{V: PointerValue{...}} with T nil. In X_objectInfo, declaredTypeName(v) then fails the *PointerType assertion and returns "" at once, so the dt.PkgPath+"."+Name concat and the fourth non-empty Go2GnoValue string never run. The realm lookup is also warmed (tx.GetPackageRealm), so GetRealmByID is always a cache hit. A gno call always carries T, so native_gas.go's line 'the stamped path sets the price' rests on a bench that leaves out part of the stamped path

candidates.evidence: reflect_bench_test.go:54 `m.Blocks[0].Values[0] = gno.TypedValue{V: gno.PointerValue{TV: &hiv.Value, Base: hiv}}` (no T); reflect.go:133-135 `pt, ok := t.(*gno.PointerType); if !ok { return "" }`

candidates.summary: the address preimage writes PkgID with the debug Stringer's spelling, `RID%X` uppercase, while Object.ID() returns lowercase hex with no prefix, so hashing "objectid:" + ID() as the ADR reads gives a different address
candidates.failure_scenario: ADR section 1 says the address hashes `objectid:<pkgid>:<newtime>`, and reflect.gno says addr is 'derived from id'. id is oid.String() = hex.EncodeToString(Hashlet) + ":" + NewTime (ownership.go MarshalAmino, lowercase, no prefix). The preimage uses oid.PkgID.String() = fmt.Sprintf("RID%X", ...) (realm.go:74-76). An indexer or wallet that derives an object's address from Object.ID() off-chain, as the ADR describes, gets a different g1 address, and nothing tells it the address is wrong. The godoc names the PkgID encoding as consensus state, yet that encoding comes from a debug Stringer. The filetests' golden g1 addresses pin today's spelling, so CI catches a later change. This is shared with #6139's preimage, so the parent reconciles the two
candidates.verify_by: go test snippet: compare crypto.AddressFromPreimage([]byte("objectid:"+oid.String())) against gno.DeriveObjectCryptoAddr(oid) for oid {PkgIDFromPkgPath("gno.land/r/demo/reflectid"), 8}: expect them to differ; read realm.go:74 and ownership.go:47-49 for the two spellings
candidates.evidence: realm.go:74-76 `return fmt.Sprintf("RID%X", pid.Hashlet[:])`; ownership.go MarshalAmino `pid := hex.EncodeToString(oid.PkgID.Hashlet[:]); return fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", pid, oid.NewTime)`; ADR line 51 `objectid:<pkgid>:<newtime>`

candidates.summary: X_objectInfo follows DeriveObjectCryptoAddr's godoc and guards only IsFinalized, but the callee also panics with a bare Go panic on a zero PkgID, which IsFinalized does not cover
candidates.failure_scenario: DeriveObjectCryptoAddr panics on `!oid.IsFinalized() || oid.PkgID.IsZero()`, and its godoc tells callers to check IsFinalized instead of relying on the panic. A stamped ID with a zero PkgID would pass X_objectInfo's guard and raise an uncatchable Go panic out of a user-callable native. That shape is unreachable on chain today: assignNewObjectID sets PkgID before NewTime (realm.go:1995-2003). So the second half of the guard is dead for this caller, and the godoc's 'use IsFinalized' advice covers only half of it
candidates.verify_by: grep every SetNewTime/SetObjectID site in gnovm/pkg/gnolang for one that stamps NewTime with a zero PkgID: realm.go:2031 and :2041 only, both after the PkgID fix-up at :1995
candidates.evidence: realm.go:1995-2003 `if oid.PkgID.IsZero() { oo.SetPkgID(rlm.ID) ... }` precedes the only SetNewTime calls at :2031/:2041
